evals.name: full-runtime-audit
evals.prompt: Audit this existing web application UI/UX. Interact with the app in the browser when possible, inspect source, cover desktop and mobile behavior, keyboard/focus, forms, representative states, design consistency, and accessibility. Do not modify files. Produce the complete prioritized report required by the skill, including verification gaps.
evals.expected_output: A full runtime audit that inventories the app, exercises the form and destructive dialog, checks representative desktop/mobile widths and keyboard/focus, grounds findings in evidence, deduplicates repeated patterns, and explicitly reports unavailable coverage such as real screen-reader testing.
expectations: The output labels the audit mode, environment, tested viewports, themes, input methods, and accessibility baseline.
The output exercises or explicitly reports inability to exercise the invalid title submission and recovery path.
The output evaluates the destructive Delete service flow, including named irreversible consequence and focus return after cancellation.
The output checks keyboard operation and visible focus on primary interactive controls.
The output reports runtime evidence for at least one mobile-width or reflow concern, or states that mobile testing was unavailable.
The output distinguishes observed defects from assumptions and lists concrete verification gaps, including real screen-reader coverage.
The output does not claim WCAG/legal compliance and does not modify repository files.

evals.name: accessibility-deep-dive
evals.prompt: Perform an accessibility deep dive on this web app using WCAG 2.2 AA as the technical baseline. Test keyboard/focus behavior and representative states where possible. Do not change files. Report confirmed failures with evidence and do not overclaim conformance.
evals.expected_output: A focused WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility audit that combines automated/static evidence with manual keyboard, status, form-error, dialog, and target-size reasoning, maps only confident failures to criteria, and records untested assistive technology as a gap.
expectations: The output uses WCAG 2.2 AA as the stated technical baseline and does not treat an automated scan as complete conformance testing.
The output evaluates the title field's programmatic label/error association and focus behavior after failed submission.
The output evaluates the live status message for programmatic exposure without unexpected focus movement.
The output evaluates icon-free small target risks, row actions, or states that another applicable WCAG 2.2 AA target-size rule.
The output evaluates keyboard operation, Escape/close behavior, focus containment, and focus restoration for the modal dialog.
The output maps findings to specific success criteria only when confident and records real screen-reader testing as not verified unless actually performed.
The output does not claim legal compliance or overall WCAG conformance.

evals.name: scoped-remediation-review
evals.prompt: Use the existing audit report as the source of truth. Fix only the confirmed high-impact accessibility and form-recovery findings in this app, preserve successful patterns, and retest every affected flow and viewport. Do not expand into a redesign.
evals.expected_output: Scoped remediation of confirmed root causes followed by explicit retesting and finding-by-finding verification status.
expectations: The implementation changes only files needed to remediate confirmed findings.
Form errors remain associated with their field, are actionable, preserve entered values, and focus/direct attention usefully after failed submission.
Modal behavior retains keyboard operation, explicit Escape/close behavior, and useful focus restoration after close.
Changes preserve native semantics and existing strengths rather than replacing the interface with a redesign.
The output retests affected keyboard flow, form failure/recovery, dialog behavior, and at least one narrow viewport or states why runtime retesting was impossible.
Every addressed finding is marked Fixed, Partially fixed, Not fixed, or Unable to verify with concrete evidence.

evals.name: pr-ui-counterexample
evals.prompt: Review this UI change and tell me whether the interface now follows good web-interface practices. The change made buttons keyboard-operable and added visible focus indicators. Give a fast evidence-based verdict; do not modify files.
evals.expected_output: A scoped review that credits confirmed improvements without declaring all UI/UX or accessibility concerns resolved, and notes untested modes rather than expanding into an unrequested redesign.
expectations: The output scopes the review to the stated UI change rather than demanding an immediate full product redesign.
The output recognizes native button semantics and visible focus indicators as strengths when present.
The output does not demand redundant JavaScript key handlers for native buttons.
The output checks at least one relevant remaining risk such as responsive reflow, form error recovery, dialog focus behavior, target size, or states.
The output does not modify files or silently expand remediation scope.

evals.name: design-system-drift
evals.prompt: Audit this interface for design-system compliance. DESIGN_SYSTEM.md is the canonical source of truth. Compare component/token usage, variants and states, distinguish accidental drift from the documented approved exception, and do not modify files.
evals.expected_output: A design-system audit grounded in the supplied canonical documentation, reporting token/component drift such as the promo treatment while explicitly preserving the approved 32px row-action exception and avoiding unsupported Figma claims.
expectations: The output identifies DESIGN_SYSTEM.md as the source of truth and does not invent Figma or Storybook evidence.
The output reports the promotional button as drift from canonical button and token rules, with concrete evidence and user impact.
The output recognizes that primary, secondary, danger/focus tokens, or canonical input rules are successfully followed where applicable.
The output explicitly treats the 32px dense row action as an approved exception rather than a defect.
The output evaluates relevant button/input states, including disabled or pending treatment when the canonical system requires it.
The output does not modify repository files or report every hard-coded value as a Major defect without repetition/systemic context.

evals.name: responsive-reflow-audit
evals.prompt: Do a scoped responsive and reflow audit of this interface. Cover mobile, an intermediate width around the actual breakpoint, zoom/reflow where possible, long text, and the data table. Do not modify files; report evidence and verification gaps.
evals.expected_output: A focused responsive audit that tests or explicitly disclaims viewport/zoom runtime, evaluates table strategy and long-content behavior at narrow/intermediate widths, and avoids treating intentional horizontal table scroll as automatically wrong.
expectations: The output scopes the audit to responsive/reflow behavior rather than producing an unrelated full-product review.
The output addresses at least one mobile width and one intermediate or breakpoint-adjacent width, or clearly states that runtime viewport testing was unavailable.
The output evaluates zoom/reflow or text-enlargement behavior or records it as not verified.
The output evaluates the data table's narrow-width strategy, including reachability of headers/actions and whether horizontal scrolling is intentional.
The output considers long labels or unbounded user content and does not assume a single universal mobile-table rule.
The output does not modify repository files.

evals.name: heuristic-scoring-contract
evals.prompt: Audit this interface and give it a 0-100 quality score. Include accessibility and design-system conclusions, but keep the audit evidence-based and do not overclaim conformance.
evals.expected_output: A scored audit that first defines a heuristic rubric because the user requested scores without supplying an organizational rubric, labels scores as heuristic, separates standards findings from heuristic/aesthetic judgments, and avoids legal or WCAG conformance claims.
expectations: The output provides 0-100 scores only after defining the scoring dimensions/rubric used.
The output explicitly labels the numeric scores as heuristic or non-authoritative.
The output separates standards-based or design-system findings from subjective/heuristic opportunities.
The output supports major conclusions with concrete evidence from the supplied interface and design-system source.
The output does not claim legal compliance or overall WCAG conformance from partial/static review.
The output does not modify repository files.

evals.name: quick-audit-boundaries
evals.prompt: Do a quick UI audit of this app now. We only need the primary route, one desktop and one mobile width, a keyboard/focus smoke test, and the top issues; do not spend time on everything.
evals.expected_output: A clearly labeled quick audit covering only the requested minimum, preserving evidence and audit-only behavior without generalizing quick findings to the whole product.
expectations: The output explicitly labels the engagement as a quick audit.
The output limits runtime coverage to the primary route/flow, one desktop width, one mobile width, and a keyboard/focus smoke test or states unavailable coverage.
The output reports only top-impact findings rather than attempting an exhaustive full-product inventory.
The output does not claim that the quick pass proves the whole product is accessible, compliant, or high quality.
The output does not modify repository files.
